problem: Learning-based object navigation policies keep parameters fixed at deployment, lack explicit long-term spatial-semantic memory, depend on viewpoint-ambiguous relations, and so revisit uninformative regions and fall into cyclic behavior across repeated episodes.
motivation: Humans find objects by combining perception, memory of where they have looked, and semantic expectations, and update hypotheses as they explore. Robots with egocentric partial observability need a similar evolving internal model to accumulate environment-specific knowledge and learn from past failures, especially in long-term, multi-episode deployment.
key_idea: Extend a standard A3C object-goal navigation pipeline with viewpoint-dependent context features, an online-updated environment-specific dynamic knowledge graph (GCN), and a training-free historical trajectory correction that suppresses revisited states and repeated actions.
insight: Ablations show the context module (CLR) causes the largest drop when removed, then ADKG and SIE. A fully dynamic graph (FDG-Net) beats static or hybrid graphs. Viewpoint-dependent cues (cos θ, e^-d) beat viewpoint-invariant semantic similarity. The correction is parameter-free and applied only at evaluation, and gains are larger on long trajectories (L≥5); it also improves MJOLNIR-o, so it is architecture-agnostic.
method: Context Learning and Reasoning (CLR): builds a 6-D per-object context vector [visibility, xc, yc, bbox area, cos θ, e^-d] between each object and the target, stacked into a 101×6 matrix and updated as the robot moves

Adaptive Dynamic Knowledge Graph (ADKG): nodes are objects, edges are e^-d spatial distances from real-time observations, gated (β_ij) with historical adjacency so memory persists across views; 3-layer GCN with GloVe node features and visibility matrix, fused with the context matrix
Semantic Information Extraction (SIE): ResNet-18 features (512×7×7), point-wise conv to 16×7×7, self-attention over 49 positions
Navigation policy: A3C (LSTM actor-critic) with GAE, parent-object auxiliary reward (Rp = Rt·Pr(t|p)·k), -0.01 step penalty, trained end-to-end in AI2-THOR

Historical trajectory optimization: Correction1 resamples actions whose predicted next state is already visited; Correction2 restricts sampling to untried actions in the current state; no trainable parameters, applied only at test time

Real-world deployment: sim-trained policy on Fetch robot, with the front-end swapped for a real object detector plus depth, category mapping to AI2-THOR, Move Forward 0.6 m, 15-step limit, no fine-tuning

setting.backbone: ResNet-18 + GCN + LSTM A3C actor-critic (trained from scratch with RL); Ours-CLIP variant swaps in a CLIP visual encoder
setting.training_data: 3M episodes of online RL rollouts in AI2-THOR (20 rooms per scene type for training; 4 scene types); no extra or web data besides GloVe embeddings
setting.observation: egocentric RGB (plus object detections; real robot uses RGB-D 640×480 with depth for object distance)
setting.action_space: discrete: MoveAhead 0.25 m, RotateLeft/Right 45°, LookUp/Down 30°, Done (real robot: Move Forward 0.6 m)
setting.privileged: none stated (object detection/labels from the AI2-THOR simulator in simulation; a real detector in real world)

numbers_note: Most simulation results appear only in bar-chart figures (Fig. 2A–D); the numbers above are from figure text labels and prose. The unseen-set SR for Correction2 in the figure text is ambiguous (81.7 all; 73.8 L≥5). Real-world numbers (Fig. 3B) are garbled in extraction; only relative gains are stated (+46.25% SR and +27.47% SPL vs human teleoperation MCRGB, -1.19 m DTS). Group II baseline numbers are not extractable.
results: HM-Nav outperforms 17 baselines (e.g. HOGN-TVGN, SSAFN, TDANet) on AI2-THOR: 81.8 SR / 36.5 SPL unseen vs HOGN-TVGN 80.6 SR, and up to 83.9 SR with Correction1. On the real Fetch robot it beats human teleoperation (MCRGB) and MJOLNIR-o, and performance improves across repeated episodes. The correction also lifts MJOLNIR-o (SR 63.7 → 69.1).
limitations: Relies only on visual cues, so it is vulnerable to severe occlusion and low light; the knowledge graph suffers error propagation from initial inaccurate detections/misclassification

Benchmarked only on AI2-THOR (no Habitat/HM3D or other standard ObjectNav benchmarks) and small real-world tests (4 scenes, 5 targets, 15-step limit); no foundation-model/LLM integration beyond a preliminary CLIP variant
SPL trades off against SR in Target Group II (SPL slightly lower than baselines)
